samples.summary: `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` (80-char `code` truncation) is a new bound with no test
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:162 slices `body.error.code` to `MAX_UPSTREAM_CODE` (80). upstream-error.test.ts covers the message cap ('caps a huge `message` on the envelope path', line 131-137) and the body cap ('drops sibling fields once the envelope stops being small'), but I found no test feeding a code longer than 80 chars — grepping the new test file for `repeat(` yields only `'x'.repeat(5000)` (message) and `'y'.repeat(6000)` (stack). If the `.slice` were removed, every test still passes.

samples.summary: Envelope with a `code` but no `message` key exercises an untested branch of `safeEnvelope`
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` guards on `'message' in body.error`, so `{error:{code:'X'}}` is forwarded without synthesizing `HTTP <status>`. Every envelope fixture in upstream-error.test.ts carries a message (ENVELOPE at line 31, `{code:'X',message:'m',command:...}` at line 69, the cap tests at 133/143/155). No case pins the message-less shape, so a change to that branch (e.g. always injecting `HTTP <status>`) would be silently accepted.

samples.summary: Only the `sheets cells` dry-run call sites are tested; the other ~10 changed `printDryRun` sites have no encoding coverage, and printDryRun's own guard cannot catch a forgotten `seg()` on a slash-bearing id
samples.evidence: dry-run.test.ts registers only `registerCellsCommand` (line 40) and asserts encoding for `cells set` / `cells batch`. The diff also adds `seg()` to dry-run paths in docs.ts (rename/delete/content), notes.ts, slides.ts, files.ts, tabs.ts, sheets-import.ts, and to docs/import.ts, notes/import.ts, slides/import.ts. `assertNoDotSegments` only rejects `.`/`..`, so a call site that dropped `seg()` on an id like `a/b/../c` (or `../x` embedded in a longer segment) would still print a walked-out URL with no test failing. The existing import dry-run tests (packages/cli/test/docs-import.test.ts:356) assert `'/documents/doc-existing/content'`, a value that is identical with or without `seg()`.

samples.summary: `downloadFileDocument`'s switch from `encodeURIComponent` to `seg()` is untested at the HttpClient level
samples.evidence: The 'request paths pin every id to one segment' block in upstream-error.test.ts covers deleteDocument, setCell, renameTab and the workspace, but not `downloadFileDocument`. Grepping the test dir for `downloadFileDocument` finds only stubs of the method (files-download.test.ts:119-154, upstream-error.test.ts:823) — the real URL is never observed, so the new dot-segment refusal on a file download id has no coverage.

samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts:106-125 exercises fetchDocument, renameDocument, copyDocument and deleteDocument with a traversal id; `moveDocument` (documents.ts:88, also changed to `seg(id)`) is never called in the file — grepping documents.test.ts shows only `moveDocuments` (plural, the bulk endpoint) at line 27.

samples.summary: Encoding assertions build a RegExp from a string containing unescaped `.`, so the dots match any character
samples.evidence: `const encoded = "..%2F..%2Fworkspaces%2F..."` is interpolated into `new RegExp(...)` at lines 115-118 without escaping; each `.` is a regex wildcard, so a URL segment like `XY%2FZW%2Fworkspaces...` would also satisfy the assertion. The check still fails on a genuinely unencoded id (it requires the literal `%2F`), so this weakens rather than voids the test, but the same value is compared with `toContain` at line 121, which is exact — the regex form is the loose one.
